title: Patate in Tegame
subtitle: Pan-cooked potatoes with rosemary, garlic, and olive oil
excerpt: Potatoes cooked slowly in a lidded pan with rosemary and garlic until soft inside and golden at the edges. Simple and good with anything.
sourceNotes: Italian home cooking tradition of one-pan potato cookery, common across central and southern regions.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Reheat in a dry pan over a medium heat to bring back the crispness on the edges.

content.text: Patate in tegame are cooked covered for most of the time, then uncovered at the end so the edges catch and crisp. Use a floury potato so the inside turns fluffy. Do not stir too often or the pieces break up.
Heat the olive oil in a wide frying pan over a medium heat. Add the garlic and rosemary. Let them sizzle for 1 minute.
Add the potato chunks. Season well with salt and pepper. Stir to coat in the oil.
Pour in the water. Put the lid on and cook on a medium-low heat for 25 minutes. Shake the pan gently every 8 minutes.
Remove the lid. Increase the heat to medium. Cook for 10 to 12 minutes more, turning the potatoes once or twice, until the edges are golden.
Taste and adjust seasoning. Remove the rosemary sprigs and garlic before serving.

items.symptom: The potatoes are catching on the base before they are cooked through.
items.cause: The heat is too high or there is not enough water.
items.fix: Add another 50ml of water and turn the heat down. Replace the lid for 5 more minutes.

items.symptom: The potatoes are soft but have no colour.
items.cause: The lid was left on for too long and too much steam built up.
items.fix: Remove the lid and raise the heat to medium-high. Cook uncovered until the water evaporates and the edges start to catch.

items.symptom: The chunks break apart when stirring.
items.cause: The potatoes were stirred too often while still firm.
items.fix: Shake the pan gently rather than stirring. Only turn the pieces once they are nearly cooked.
